newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money rates firm slightly.
newsitem.headline: German call money rates firm slightly.

text.p: German call money rates firmed slighty on Monday to trade in a broad range of 3.00 to 3.08 percent after 3.03 to 3.05 percent on Friday.
Some banks said demand for cash had increased a little but added that rates may well slip back to 3.00/3.05 percent by the afternoon.

Dealers said the flotation of telephone giant Deutsche Telekom AG had not yet affected the money market but could cause problems on Wednesday when 20 billion marks flow out of bank accounts and into Telekom's coffers -- a massive shift of funds that could cause a surge in market volatility.

"It will definitely be volatile on Wednesday," one money dealer said. Commercial banks' effective deposits at the Bundesbank slipped to 37.4 billion marks on Friday from 38.3 billion marks on Thursday.
The average for the month through Sunday was 39.3 billion marks, down from 39.8 billion. Lombard borrowings totalled about 100 million marks on Friday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was 3.05817 percent on Monday, compared with 3.05300 percent on Friday. --Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
